facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 木_偏财 (Wood carrying The Horizon). Persona The Horizon (偏财). Definition line: "Wide-ranging engagement, opportunity sensed at a distance". Keyword Reach, charge dynamic, poles catalyst Momentum / friction Scatter. Family function: Action. Cost dimension: opportunity sensed far off; the near things blur. Arena: horizon, wind, open road, far light, the next place. Classical portrait: wide-ranging engagement; opportunity sensed at a distance; windfall, generosity, the near things blur. Ruled domains: Opportunity, Ventures, Father. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 正财.
Element arena: Wood (trunk, branch, root, grain, growth, the forest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Metal. structural_interaction seed: "Metal directing Wood broadly — precision ranging across living material".
- k2_overview: "Your Wood moves as the Horizon: growth that reaches for distant light. Opportunity, for you, is territory: new markets, new cities, branches extended where no one from home has grown. You expand naturally and prune reluctantly. Fortune arrives through the reaching. Roots decide how much of it you keep."
- k2_functional: "You grow toward opportunity steadily, extending reach every season without retreating."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Wide-branching","Deal-maker","Open-handed"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Opportunity":"Opportunities appear to you as open land: markets unplanted, niches unclaimed. You see fertile ground others call wilderness. Scout it, but check the soil before transplanting everything.","Ventures":"Your ventures grow in groves: several trunks sharing a root system of skills and contacts. Let each mature before seeding the next. Orchards fail from planting fever, not planting.","Father":"The father-thread runs green and rangy: reach, enterprise, restlessness, wherever a paternal figure stood. Where that reaching shaped you, keep it. Where it left no roots, plant them yourself."}
- fn_reading.friction.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.friction; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 木_正财 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Cultivating","Compounding","Deep-rooted"],"friction":["Stuck","Plays it safe","Inflexible"]}
- Sibling cell 木_正财 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Outgrowing a place and staying anyway is a pattern of yours, and calling it loyalty stopped being accurate a while ago. The ground you hold has long since stopped feeding you. Holding it anyway is the habit, and the habit never checks the yield."

Core element Metal, energy element Wood. Law: Metal tames Wood (金克木: the knife prunes the branch). Relative to the core the energy is the tamed, so Wood is this core's Action. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Metal core that shows Wood on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Wood as the Action is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 金_木's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Whatever is newest in front of you is what you chase hardest. You have more Wood than strength behind it, so you chase the fresh start ahead of the finish. Keep in mind that the half-done thing behind you was once what you chased.

value_b.text: The first week of anything is the one you chase. Since the new shows no flaws, you chase it ahead of finishing the old. You know by now that the new has the same flaws waiting, so chasing it costs more than finishing.

value.text: Where you are is rarely what you chase. Because staying feels like being stuck rather than home, you chase the far plan with hours the near one needed. Remember that each chase costs you the venture already begun, and half a venture pays nothing.

value.text: Chasing the next thing keeps you alive. Since the new chance pulls more than the promised one, you chase it and leave the unfinished half to your partner. You promised them the middle as well as the start, remember, whatever you chase now.

value.text: Spreading yourself over several things feels normal, and one alone feels like being caught. Your Wood outruns the strength carrying it, so you spread across every open option rather than drop one. Remember how thin that spreads you, one body over all of them.

value_b.text: You spread over the next thing as easily as the first. Since every open option feels like safety, you spread across half chances rather than hold a whole one. Do not forget that chances come easily, and strength for one is what spreading costs.

value.text: You are spread among more things than your body keeps up with. Letting go feels like losing rather than choosing, so you spread yourself over them, tired at each one. Spread this thin, you never get a full rest, and that is worth remembering.

value.text: Whenever something new asks for you, you spread yourself one slice thinner. Since closing an option feels like losing, you keep spreading rather than shut one. You hand your partner and family the same thin slice as everything else, and you know it.

value.text: Unspent money feels less real to you than money already gone. Spending keeps life feeling open, so you spend an easy month rather than put any toward a slow one. Bear in mind that you meet the slow month too, with everything already spent.

value_b.text: You spend money as if it were made to move. Money held back feels like life held back, so you spend it today rather than save for a day you have not met. You already know how early you spend the quiet months.

value.text: With money, you spend sooner than you let it sit. Since spending feels like living and saving like waiting, you spend the month's money ahead of keeping any. You pay for the free spending in money never kept, as every thin month reminds you.

value.text: Spending on the people near you comes before your own next month. Helping them out feels better than keeping, so you spend on their short months rather than a shared cushion. Never forget that you spend their quiet months as well as your own.
